reasons.business: Crowded screen-time and habit market with free built-in alternatives; no monetisation design; generic name; vocabulary close to one anime franchise; no real-user evidence (capped at 6).
reasons.pmf: Plausible fit for evening doomscrollers via the Focus System; weak for Fitness and Personality honour-checkbox packs; only the owner's own trial, no retention or interview data.
reasons.technical: Pure, deterministic, well-tested rules engine (235 Flutter + 16 JVM tests pass, 81.9% line coverage, format and analyze clean). But: the release artefacts are the pre-fix build, there is a wrongful-penalty path, rule-softening loopholes exist, native enforcement on Android 15+ is unproven, foreground-service start failures are silent, and there are no device or integration tests.
reasons.uiux: Distinctive, coherent HUD and System voice; reduced motion respected. Over 100 labels at 9-11 px, no large-text tests, long onboarding without a lock-time choice, a confusing 00:00:00 empty penalty state, and a nightly watcher notification plus a daily verdict redirect even when nothing is owed.
reasons.security: No INTERNET permission, minimal and justified permissions, non-exported components, local-only data, signing keys git-ignored, prominent disclosure present. The shipped build lacks allowBackup=false, which contradicts the privacy policy; reflections are exported without a warning.
reasons.behavioural: Penalties are bounded, expire, and come with an emergency exit, releases, a contest and a dry run (in code, not in the shipped build). A binary all-or-nothing verdict, punitive framing, the doubled 8-hour Dungeon lock and punished unverifiable social tasks risk frustration and quitting.
reasons.retention: A strong daily ritual for committed users, but a punishment-led loop, near-miss failures and nightly friction suggest high early churn; no data to show otherwise.
reasons.publication: A P0 is open: the AAB the release kit says to upload is the unsafe pre-fix build. The FGS specialUse, Health apps, Data safety and target audience declarations are not submitted; the 12-tester, 14-day closed test has not started; device behaviour is unverified (capped at 7).

findings.title: Release artefacts in dist/ are the pre-fix build (doubling carry-over penalty, no 18+ or health gate, backup enabled) with the same versionCode 13, and the release kit says to upload them
findings.fix: Remove the stale artefacts, bump to 0.9.1+14, rebuild from HEAD, add a release check script (aapt2 manifest check plus libapp.so fingerprint), update the kit and the owner's phone.
findings.acceptance: aapt2 shows allowBackup=false; libapp.so contains 'penalty_expired' and 'I AM 18 OR OLDER' and not 'carried_over'; versionCode > 13; the release kit names the new file.

findings.title: A rest-period edit on a failing day shrinks the next 4-hour lock to 30 minutes; softening edits are absent from the report
findings.fix: Rest-period and lock-time edits apply only to locks on days after tomorrow; require a waking window of at least 12 h; list sleep_changed, lock_start_changed, system_switched, reduction_set, block_app_removed, cap_unmeasured and penalty_expired in the report's honesty section.
findings.acceptance: Probe 1 yields a 240-minute lock; a waking window under 12 h is refused by test; a report test shows each softening event.

findings.title: Wrongful penalty: a screen-time cap measured as kept becomes a failure (240-min lock plus 60-min debt) when the meter returns null at judging
findings.fix: Use the last in-app reading after 20:00 if present; otherwise mark the item unmeasured with no lock or debt, and log it and show it in the report.
findings.acceptance: Probe 4 passes (no QuestFailed); existing cap tests still pass.

findings.title: No device or integration evidence that locks engage, survive reboot, force stop, Doze and OEM killers
findings.fix: Add an androidx.test instrumented test for the watcher, block screen and alarm path; run and commit a device checklist on Android 13, 14, 15 and 16, including one aggressive OEM skin.
findings.acceptance: The checklist with per-version results is committed; the instrumented test passes.

findings.title: Background FGS start on Android 15+ may be refused (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW exemption needs a visible overlay; the exact-alarm exemption covers user-requested actions only) and the failure is swallowed
findings.fix: On start failure, post a high-priority notification to arm the lock and record the failure for the app to log; offer a user-visible arm action; verify on Android 15 and 16.
findings.acceptance: On an Android 15 device with the app swiped away, the lock engages at the chosen time, or a notification appears and the outage is logged.

findings.title: Play declarations (FGS specialUse plus video, Health apps, Data safety, target audience, content rating) not submitted; the 12-tester, 14-day closed test has not started
findings.fix: The owner completes App content in Play Console on the rebuilt build and starts the closed test.
findings.acceptance: Console shows App content complete; 12+ testers opted in continuously for 14 days.

findings.title: Switching System on a failing evening deletes that day's System penalty (penalty kind taken from the System active at judging)
findings.fix: Store the System with each issued quest snapshot and derive the penalty kind from it.
findings.acceptance: Probe 2 yields a Focus debt of 60 minutes.

findings.title: Abandoning at 23:55 escapes the verdict, and every new Awakening grants a fresh 3-day dry run
findings.fix: When today's quest is incomplete after 18:00, judge before archiving or refuse until the verdict; allow one dry run per install, with a flag outside the save.

findings.title: Every night the watcher FGS starts ('Watching your locked apps') and the first locked-app open is redirected to Do or Die, even when nothing is owed
findings.fix: Push today's completion state to native code; redirect and run the watcher after midnight only when the last-known quest state was incomplete or a lock is scheduled.
findings.acceptance: With a cleared day, no watcher notification appears after midnight and no redirect happens.

findings.title: Accessibility: over 100 labels at 9-11 px monospace, no 200% text-scale testing, penalty dim text at 4.49:1
findings.fix: Set a minimum of 12 sp (14 for body), add text-scale widget tests, and adjust dim colours to at least 4.5:1.
findings.acceptance: Widget tests at textScaler 2.0 show no overflow; contrast check passes.

findings.title: Scope: three Systems, two of them unverifiable honour-checkbox packs; narrow to Focus for the test
findings.fix: Ship a Focus-only tester build with the packs behind a flag.
findings.acceptance: The tester build's Awakening offers Focus only.

findings.title: Binary all-or-nothing verdict and an 8-hour doubled Dungeon lock drive near-miss frustration
findings.fix: Partial-credit threshold (for example 80% avoids the lock, no XP); cap the Dungeon lock at the normal length.
findings.acceptance: Engine tests cover the 80% day and the Dungeon lock length.

findings.title: The whole save, including an unbounded log, is re-serialised on every change; the log is scanned linearly for counters
findings.fix: Store the log separately (append-only), keep counters in state.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark test saves in under 50 ms with 5,000 log entries.

findings.title: Store screenshots outdated (Personality shown while the listing says Focus is core) and show a personal status bar and third-party app names
findings.fix: Re-shoot from the Focus build in demo mode with neutral app names; confirm the privacy policy URL is live.
findings.acceptance: Screenshots match the listing and show no third-party marks.

findings.title: A lock time after midnight inside a night owl's waking hours is moved to the next morning
findings.fix: Interpret a start minute before wake-up as the following calendar day when the waking period crosses midnight.
findings.acceptance: Probe 6 starts at 00:30 the next day.

findings.title: The reflection penalty accepts junk and invites rumination
findings.fix: Reframe as a 'plan for tomorrow' prompt; do not police the content.

findings.title: Native and Dart never-lock lists differ (Google Maps listed in the picker but silently dropped)
findings.fix: Filter the picker with the Dart list too, or generate one list for both.
findings.acceptance: Maps is absent from the picker in a widget test with a fake blocker.
